content.title: Switch time ranges and refresh portfolio performance context
content.intent: Prove that selecting any supported time-range value keeps exactly one active choice and refreshes the chart range, x-axis labels, and period comparison.
content.technique_notes: Equivalence partitioning over the segmented time-range control values. covering_array requested at strength=2 from the default non-money/auth/data-loss risk gate and degraded to effective_t=1 because only one input varied; enumerated representatives were 1D, 1W, 1M, 3M, YTD, 1Y, and ALL. Budget estimate remained within the 8-pair ceiling, so all representatives stayed in scope.

content.title: Hover a performance point to inspect the custom tooltip
content.intent: Prove hovering a chart point shows the custom tooltip near the active point, updates the displayed date, portfolio value, benchmark value, and return, and leaves summary cards unchanged.
content.technique_notes: State/flow applied because the chart moves from unhovered to hovered state and the outcome includes both newly visible hover data and a non-changing dashboard summary. Negative/error reasoning applied to the forbidden summary-card drift and forbidden default-tooltip behavior.

content.title: Lock and unlock a selected performance point by clicking it
content.intent: Prove a chart point click locks selection with persistent point, tooltip, and lock icon, and a second click on the same point unlocks it.
content.technique_notes: State/flow applied because the interaction traverses unlocked → locked → unlocked chart states. No combinatorial expansion was needed because the source defines one interaction family rather than outcome-changing value classes.

content.title: Clear the selected performance point when the time range changes
content.intent: Prove changing the time range clears any previously selected chart point after a lock has been established.
content.technique_notes: State/flow applied because the path verifies the cross-state reset from locked selection to cleared selection when another control changes chart context. Equivalence partitioning applied to use a representative time-range change rather than mint separate scenarios for each destination value because the expected outcome is the same cleared-selection state.

content.title: Load portfolio performance with the 1M default selection
content.intent: Prove the overview opens with the supported time-range options visible, 1M active by default, and the required chart structure present.
content.technique_notes: Presence and absolute checks from straightforward source-backed defaults and static chart composition. No boundary, security, perf, or i18n expansion applied because the source for this use-case states neither input bounds nor those behavior families.

content.title: Clear a locked performance point with Escape
content.intent: Prove the Escape key clears a locked chart-point selection after the point has been locked.
content.technique_notes: State/flow applied because the path verifies a keyboard-driven transition from locked to cleared state. I kept this as an edge path rather than an a11y path because the source promises the Escape behavior itself but does not state broader keyboard-accessibility requirements.

content.title: Leave the performance chart to dismiss hover details
content.intent: Prove pointer exit hides the tooltip after a hover interaction has displayed it.
content.technique_notes: State/flow applied because the path verifies the transition from visible hover details back to the resting chart state. Negative/error reasoning applied because the required outcome is the absence of the tooltip after pointer exit.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Ranked highest because incorrect time-range switching corrupts the main analytical task and exercises three invariant promises at once across every supported period.
[value_score] Ranked next because tooltip content and summary-card stability are central to interpreting the chart and interactive hover regressions are common.
[value_score] Ranked high because lock/unlock state combines multiple visible obligations and is easy to break in custom chart interaction code.
[value_score] Ranked above default-load coverage because stale locked state after a range change would mislead analysis across periods.
[value_score] Ranked mid-pack because defaults and structural rendering matter on first load but are less stateful than interaction paths.
[value_score] Ranked below click lock/unlock because Escape clearing is a secondary interaction path with a narrower trigger.
[value_score] Ranked lowest because tooltip dismissal is important but isolated to the hover exit condition and exercises fewer promises than the other paths.
